proof:
Source. Step 4 of the supplied proof of the parent — (4a) the variation field Z = ζν, (4b) the second variation (Simon Ch. 2, 5.4, with Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.12 (‡)), (4c) the extension to locally Lipschitz ζ — together with the items of its step 3 on the second fundamental form (D_τν ∈ T_xM, B = hν, |A|² = Σ_i|D_{τ_i}ν|², symmetry by Simon 4.26). Departure: Simon's Lemma 5.11 is used in the pointwise form valid for a variation with zero acceleration, normal initial velocity and H ≡ 0, derived directly from the Taylor expansion of J_t (Simon 5.2–5.4); this needs neither (closure(M) ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅ nor stationarity (Lemma 5.11 uses stationarity only to drop ∫div_M of the acceleration, which is 0 here). Sibling lemmas: area_formula (Submission.codim1_hcp_submanifold_area_formula), lipschitz_approx (Submission.codim1_hcp_lipschitz_smooth_approx), smooth_charts (Submission.codim1_hcp_smooth_charts), chart_tangent_space, locally_closed.

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]; T_x := tangentSpace M x and P_x its orthogonal projection (for x ∈ M, T_x is an m-dimensional subspace by chart_tangent_space, so span T_x = T_x); D_τν := Dν(x)τ; for a linear functional ℓ, |ℓ|²_{T_x} := Σ_j ℓ(P_xe_j)².

0. (Second fundamental form.)
 (0.1) For x ∈ M, T_x ⊆ A₀ (velocities of C¹ curves in M ⊆ A₀ lie in the closed subspace A₀), so A₀ = T_x ⊕ ℝν(x) orthogonally.
 (0.2) For x ∈ M and τ ∈ T_x, D_τν ∈ T_x. Take a C¹ curve γ in M with γ(0) = x and γ'(0) = τ; ν∘γ is differentiable at 0 with derivative D_τν (ν is differentiable at x ∈ O). Since ν(γ(s)) ∈ A₀ and |ν(γ(s))|² = 1 for all s, D_τν ∈ A₀ and ν(x)·D_τν = 0, so D_τν ∈ T_x by (0.1).
 (0.3) (Symmetry, Simon 4.26.) η·D_τν = τ·D_ην for τ, η ∈ T_x. Take a C^∞ chart (V, W, ψ) at x (smooth_charts), x = ψ(v₀). For v ∈ V, ∂_iψ(v) ∈ T_{ψ(v)} (chart_tangent_space), so ν(ψ(v))·∂_iψ(v) = 0. Differentiating in v_j: (Dν(ψ(v))∂_jψ(v))·∂_iψ(v) + ν(ψ(v))·∂_j∂_iψ(v) = 0. The second term is symmetric in (i, j), hence so is the first; at v₀ the ∂_iψ(v₀) form a basis of T_x, and bilinearity gives the claim.
 (0.4) (Hilbert–Schmidt identity.) For a linear map L from ℝ^P to ℝ^P or to ℝ and an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x: Σ_j|L(P_xe_j)|² = trace(P_xL*LP_x) = trace(L*LP_x) = Σ_i|Lτ_i|² (P_x² = P_x and the trace formula trace(P_xS) = Σ_iτ_i·Sτ_i). Hence |A|²(x) = Σ_i|D_{τ_i}ν|². With h_ij := −τ_j·D_{τ_i}ν (= h_ji by (0.3)), (0.2) gives D_{τ_i}ν = −Σ_jh_ijτ_j, so |A|²(x) = Σ_{i,j}h_ij², and Σ_ih_ii = −trace(P_xDν(x)) = 0 by hypothesis. If ζ is differentiable within M at x, its derivative is unique on T_x (T_x is spanned by velocities of C¹ curves in M through x) and |∇^Mζ|²(x) = |d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} = Σ_i(d^M_xζ(τ_i))².
 (0.5) |A|² is continuous on M (Dν is continuous on O, and x ↦ P_x is continuous on M: in a chart, P_{ψ(v)} = Dψ(v)(Dψ(v)*Dψ(v))^{-1}Dψ(v)*, and ψ^{-1} is continuous on W ∩ M by properness and injectivity). M is Borel (locally_closed, part (a)).

1. (B.1 for smooth ζ̃.) Let ζ̃ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ and C' ⊆ M compact with ζ̃ = 0 on M ∖ C'. We show
 (1.0) ∫_M |A|²ζ̃² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x} dH^m.
 (1a) The variation field (parent 4a). C' is a compact subset of the open set O ∩ U; choose β ∈ C^∞_c(O ∩ U; [0, 1]) with β = 1 on a neighbourhood of C'. Let Z₀ := βζ̃ν on O and Z₀ := 0 off O; Z₀ is C^∞ on ℝ^P because it vanishes on the open complement of the compact set tsupport β ⊆ O. Put Z := Π∘Z₀ with Π the orthogonal projection onto A₀. Then Z is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport Z ⊆ tsupport β ⊆ U, and Z takes values in A₀. For x ∈ M: if β(x) = 1 then Z(x) = ζ̃(x)Πν(x) = ζ̃(x)ν(x); if β(x) ≠ 1 then x ∉ C', so ζ̃(x) = 0 = Z(x). Hence Z = ζ̃ν on M.
 (1b) For x ∈ M and τ ∈ T_x, with γ as in (0.2): DZ(x)τ = (Z∘γ)'(0) = ((ζ̃∘γ)·(ν∘γ))'(0) = (Dζ̃(x)τ)ν(x) + ζ̃(x)D_τν.
 (1c) Second variation. Let K := tsupport Z (a compact subset of U), Λ := sup‖DZ‖ and Φ_t := id + tZ. For |t| < 1/(1 + Λ), Φ_t is C^∞ and injective with injective derivative I + tDZ (the mean value inequality gives |Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| ≥ (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b|). By area_formula with E := M ∩ K (Borel, ⊆ M),
 f(t) := H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^m, J_t(x) := √det(b_ij(t)),
 where, for an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_m of T_x and DZ = DZ(x), b_ij(t) := (τ_i + tDZτ_i)·(τ_j + tDZτ_j) = δ_ij + tc_ij + t²d_ij with c_ij := τ_i·DZτ_j + τ_j·DZτ_i and d_ij := DZτ_i·DZτ_j (b(t) is the matrix of (DΦ_t(x)ι_x)*(DΦ_t(x)ι_x) in the basis τ). det(b(t)) is a polynomial in t whose coefficients are bounded in terms of m and Λ, and det(b(0)) = 1; so there is t₁ ∈ (0, 1/(1 + Λ)) with det(b(t)) ≥ 1/2 and |∂_t^kJ_t(x)| ≤ C_k (k ≤ 3) for |t| ≤ t₁ and all x ∈ M. J_t is continuous on M (in chart coordinates), and H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ (K is a compact subset of U). By differentiation under the integral sign (twice, with dominants C₂ and C₃), F(t) := ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^m is C² on (−t₁, t₁), f(t) = ENNReal.ofReal(F(t)) there, and F''(0) = ∫_{M∩K} ∂_t²J_t|_{t=0} dH^m.
 Taylor expansion (Simon 5.2–5.4, initial velocity Z, zero acceleration): put a := Σ_iτ_i·DZτ_i and E := tc + t²d. From det(I + E) = 1 + trE + ½(trE)² − ½tr(E²) + O(|E|³),
 J_t² = 1 + 2at + Qt² + O(t³), Q := Σ_i|DZτ_i|² + 2a² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_j·DZτ_i)² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·DZτ_j)(τ_j·DZτ_i).
 Since Σ_i|DZτ_i|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_j·DZτ_i)² = Σ_i|(DZτ_i)^⊥|² (w^⊥ := w − P_xw) and √(1 + u) = 1 + u/2 − u²/8 + O(u³),
 ∂_t²J_t|_{t=0} = a² + Σ_i|(DZτ_i)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·DZτ_j)(τ_j·DZτ_i).
 Insert (1b), using (0.2)–(0.4):
 - a = Σ_i(Dζ̃(x)τ_i)(τ_i·ν(x)) + ζ̃(x)Σ_iτ_i·D_{τ_i}ν = 0 + ζ̃(x)·trace(P_xDν(x)) = 0;
 - (DZτ_i)^⊥ = (Dζ̃(x)τ_i)ν(x), because ζ̃(x)D_{τ_i}ν ∈ T_x; so Σ_i|(DZτ_i)^⊥|² = Σ_i(Dζ̃(x)τ_i)² = |Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x};
 - τ_i·DZτ_j = ζ̃(x)τ_i·D_{τ_j}ν = −ζ̃(x)h_ji, so Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·DZτ_j)(τ_j·DZτ_i) = ζ̃(x)²Σ_{i,j}h_jih_ij = ζ̃(x)²|A|²(x).
 Hence ∂_t²J_t(x)|_{t=0} = |Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x} − |A|²(x)ζ̃(x)² for x ∈ M ∩ K. For x ∈ M ∖ K, Z vanishes near x, so ζ̃ν = 0 on M near x and, as |ν| = 1, ζ̃ = 0 on M near x: ζ̃(x) = 0 and Dζ̃(x) = 0 on T_x. Therefore F''(0) = ∫_M (|Dζ̃(x)|²_{T_x} − |A|²ζ̃²) dH^m; both terms are Borel on M, bounded, and vanish off M ∩ K, a set of finite measure.
 (1d) Minimality. By hypothesis there is t₀ > 0 with F(0) = H^m(M ∩ K) ≤ F(t) for |t| < min(t₀, t₁). A C² function with a local minimum at 0 has F''(0) ≥ 0 (F'(0) = 0, and if F''(0) < 0 then F'' < 0 near 0 and F(t) − F(0) = ½F''(θ_tt)t² < 0 for small t ≠ 0). This is (1.0).

2. (Locally Lipschitz ζ; parent 4c.) Let ζ be locally Lipschitz on M and vanish on M ∖ C, C ⊆ M compact. M is an embedded C¹ submanifold, so lipschitz_approx applies. Its part (i) shows that x ↦ d^M_xζ(P_xe_j) is H^m-a.e. strongly measurable on M for every j, hence so are |d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} = Σ_j(d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))² and |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} for any C^∞ ζ_k. Its part (ii) gives a compact C' ⊆ M and C^∞ functions ζ_k with ζ_k = 0 on M ∖ C', ζ_k → ζ uniformly on M, and ∫⁻_M |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} dH^m → 0; by the measurability just noted, this is convergence to 0 in L¹(H^m⌞M) of these a.e.-measurable functions, i.e. Dζ_k → d^Mζ in L²(H^m⌞M) for the seminorms |·|_{T_x}. By step 1, ∫_M |A|²ζ_k² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |Dζ_k(x)|²_{T_x} dH^m for every k.
 - Left side: ζ_k² → ζ² uniformly on M, all these functions vanish on M off the compact set C ∪ C' ⊆ M, H^m(C ∪ C') < ∞ (C ∪ C' is a compact subset of U), and |A|² is bounded on C ∪ C' (0.5). So ∫_M |A|²ζ_k² dH^m → ∫_M |A|²ζ² dH^m.
 - Right side: |·|_{T_x} is a seminorm, so ||Dζ_k(x)|_{T_x} − |d^M_xζ|_{T_x}| ≤ |Dζ_k(x) − d^M_xζ|_{T_x}. The function |∇^Mζ|² = |d^M_xζ|²_{T_x} is a.e.-measurable on M by part (i) of lipschitz_approx. It is bounded: at points where ζ is differentiable within M, |d^M_xζ(τ)| ≤ L|τ| for τ ∈ T_x by the local Lipschitz bound along curves (L a Lipschitz constant of ζ on M near the compact C), at the other points fderivWithin is 0; and it vanishes at points of M ∖ C (there ζ = 0 on a neighbourhood in M, so d^M_xζ = 0 on T_x). Thus |∇^Mζ| ∈ L²(H^m⌞M), and Minkowski's inequality gives ‖|Dζ_k|_{T}‖_{L²(H^m⌞M)} → ‖|∇^Mζ|‖_{L²(H^m⌞M)}, i.e. ∫_M |Dζ_k(x)|²_{T_x} dH^m → ∫_M |∇^Mζ|² dH^m.
 Letting k → ∞ gives ∫_M |A|²ζ² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |∇^Mζ|² dH^m, where |A|²(x) = Σ_j|Dν(x)(P_xe_j)|² and |∇^Mζ|²(x) = Σ_j(d^M_xζ(P_xe_j))² as in the statement. ∎
key_steps: For x ∈ M and τ ∈ T_xM: D_τν ∈ T_xM, η·D_τν = τ·D_ην (C^∞ chart), |A|² = Σ_ij h_ij², and Σ_i h_ii = −trace(P_x Dν(x)) = 0.
For C^∞ ζ̃ vanishing on M off a compact set, Z := Π_{A₀}(βζ̃ν) is C^∞, compactly supported in U, and Z = ζ̃ν on M.
area_formula and differentiation under the integral make F(t) = H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ K)) a C² function with F''(0) = ∫ ∂_t²J_t; the Taylor expansion of J_t gives ∂_t²J_t = |∇^Mζ̃|² − |A|²ζ̃² pointwise.
The deformation hypothesis gives a local minimum at 0, hence F''(0) ≥ 0: B.1 for smooth ζ̃.
lipschitz_approx (measurability of d^Mζ, and smooth ζ_k with uniform and L² gradient convergence) and passage to the limit give B.1 for locally Lipschitz ζ with compact support in M.
